purpose: Cold displacement-based fiber-slab coupling to V11D truss, bearing and ties. Verify weak equilibrium, energy, trial rollback and discretization before any historical or global interpretation.

discretization.Lch_definition: Uniform two-point Gauss rule: Lch=element_length/2, the longitudinal quadrature weight. Each fully cracked integration band dissipates Ac*Gf. Not the fiber depth, and not proof of mesh-objective crack number or location in a distributed panel.
discretization.refinement_status: Steel16-panel topology,17connection stations,32equivalent-knuckle density and actuator physical location held fixed. Report mesh dependence; do not widen tolerances or force convergence to historical collapse.

loading.cycle_test_design: 60mm reversal chosen for a constitutive coupling test after a preliminary monotonic probe reached its first member screen near68mm. This is a disclosed test-design choice, not an independently predicted historical amplitude or a fit to observed collapse.
loading.status: Prescribed displacements relative to the solved quarter-gravity preload, artificial actuator tests NOT aircraft damage. Keep all80psf weight once on slab. Actuator reaction and work are included.

solver.policy: Trial from last committed material state, Newton with line search and cutback. Never commit rejected trials. Stop first nominal member/seat/tie screen, concrete compression or rebar strain domain, nonpositive constrained tangent, or unresolved continuation. No tie deletion, postbuckling, dynamic collapse or artificial stabilizing spring.

acceptance.classification: Implementation/analytic checks must pass. Mesh gates reported separately: failing them blocks use of that postcracked response as a converged panel prediction, not honest publication of a sensitivity diagnostic.

method_references.scope: Displacement-based shape functions yield weak section equilibrium. Own small-strain implementation, no OpenSees execution.
Prismatic section evaluations at longitudinal Gauss integration points.
Area under tensile stress-strain law Gf/crack-bandwidth. Our quadrature tributary choice is explicit and tested, not a DIANA default claimed for this beam.
